newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Resident in Japan arrested for spying for N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Resident in Japan arrested for spying for N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's intelligence agency has arrested a Korean resident in Japan for spying for North Korea, an agency spokesman said on Thursday.

He said the Agency for National Security Planning charged the man, 40-year-old travel agent Yoo Yoong-bum, on Wednesday with violating the National Security Law that bans activities benefiting the North.

The spokesman said Yoo visited South Korea nine times between 1991 and 1994 to contact a North Korean mole and collect intelligence reports. Yoo was detained on Monday one day after arriving in Seoul.

The mole, Ahn Jae-koo, a lecturer at a Seoul university, is now serving a life sentence handed out to him in 1994 for passing on information about labour movements in the South to the North, the spokesman said.
Yoo was also accused of delivering a total of 20 million yen ($170,000) to Ahn to finance his espionage operation, he added.

The spokesman declined to comment, however, on local media reports that Yoo's arrest followed a tip-off by North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop, the most senior Pyongyang official to flee his homeland.
Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue, told South Korean investigators after he arrived in Seoul in April that Pyongyang maintained a network of moles in the South, the intelligence agency said.
